craft_notes: Same song, same sthāyin (vismaya resolving into śama); verse color: acclamation — the hero named. Sanskrit is terse to the point of bluntness: four words (jayati eṣaḥ vīraḥ kulendraḥ), no verb but 'is victorious,' no ornament. Firing structures: brevity itself -> keep the L4 brutally short (padding a 4-word verse would be decoration, and decoration is the one thing this verse refuses); the source already repeats jayati from v1, so the refrain is given, not invented -> single-word echo line ('victorious.') as the close; end-weight 'victorious' (the verse IS the victory cry; it ends where it began). Dashes as chant breaths matching v1's caesuras so the two verses scan as one song. Minimal pass: reline L3 + refrain-drop second line.

lines: Victorious, this hero — the Kula's lord —

reads_against.argmap: premise (This hero, lord of the Kula, is victorious) + inference (The victorious hero is Kula's lord)
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta (wonder at Śiva's spanda) with śānta; sthayibhava vismaya resolving into śama
reads_against.l2: This hero, lord of the Kula — victorious.
l3: Victorious is this hero, the Kula's lord.
